<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Takeover of the [ORG_1] Sugar Mill Deal</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling processing network instead of school lunches.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study. Governor Victor needs to make the details public as soon as possible so people can understand the full implications. For instance, what happens to FCI contracts? Will they be assigned to the [ORG_1] Mill? Will customers have the right to choose going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can make their own crop decisions going forward. We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our bills are going to be paid in full. If the bills aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the logistics purchase in this deal? May never happen. Make it easy - just deal with the under collection through securitization and through the IEX refund to the [ORG_1] Mill and get on with it.


Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the [ORG_6] of Understanding:

• Commitment to Provide Produce: The [ORG_1] Mill will keep its current processing plants and other agricultural assets and commit them to provide processed goods on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.
• [ORG_7]: [ORG_8] will commit the entire output of their [LOC_2] facility (one of [ORG_9] non-regulated processing facilities) to the [ORG_10] on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of [LOC_2] is to be brought online by August 14, 2024. If not brought online by August 14, 2024, [ORG_8] shall be assessed a ₹1.5 crore penalty.
